# Rating

Rating component with 5 stars, supporting two variants: 1. With "Comments" label below 2. With numeric labels (1-5) above each star

Also asked as: stars, score.

**Import:** `import { Rating } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Rating/Rating.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Rating/Rating.stories.jsx` — Overview, Content, Variants, InteractionStates, Interactive, PropsRender, Unrated, Rated, Hovered, Focused, Required, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Rating/Rating.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations · Motion.

## Usage

Use a rating for a single satisfaction score out of five: the end of a session, a piece of feedback, a quick judgment the person makes in one gesture. Five items is the whole scale; there is no other length.

`variant` chooses what the row says about itself: `comments` puts one caption under the row, `numeric` puts 1 to 5 above each item. `icon` is `star` or `thumbs-up`.

## Motion

| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Stars fill as a color change, staggered 20 ms. |

## Best practices

### Use stars for quality and thumbs for approval. {#use-stars-for-quality-and-thumbs-for-approval}

Match the icon to the question.

Do: Stars rate the quality of a session.
Don't: Thumbs on a graded five-point scale.

### Start empty for new input. {#start-empty-for-new-input}

A pre-filled rating biases the answer.

Do: No rating yet, so the person gives their own.
Don't: Four stars filled before the person has rated.

### Show a given rating as disabled. {#show-a-given-rating-as-disabled}

A rating that cannot change reads as a result.

Do: A recorded rating, disabled.
Don't: A recorded rating that still looks editable.

### It is always controlled. {#it-is-always-controlled}

```jsx
// Incorrect: the component holds no state. Without an onChange the items are
// clickable and nothing ever changes.
<Rating label="How was the session?" />

// Correct: onChange receives the number, not an event.
<Rating label="How was the session?" value={score} onChange={setScore} />
```

### It submits its value under `name`. {#it-submits-its-value-under-name}

A hidden input carries the score with its form, so `name` is how a server reads it.

```jsx
<form onSubmit={submit}>
    <Rating name="score" label="Rating" value={score} onChange={setScore} />
</form>
```

### Give it a `label`. {#give-it-a-label}

Do: A label names the row, so a page with two ratings tells them apart.
Don't: Without a label the row falls back to the generic name "Rating". `commentsLabel` is a caption, not a substitute.

## Accessibility

- **It is one value out of five, and says so.** The row is a `radiogroup` and each item is a `radio` carrying `aria-checked` and an `aria-label` of "Rate 1" through "Rate 5". The chosen value is in the accessibility tree, not only in the fill color.
- **One tab stop, arrow keys within it.** Tab reaches the group once, landing on the checked item, or the first when nothing is checked; Left/Right, Up/Down, Home and End move the value. Enter and Space still activate an item directly.
- **Moving the selection is changing it.** An arrow key calls `onChange`, so a keyboard user cannot browse the scale without setting it. That is the usual radio-group behavior.
- **Disabled stays announced.** The items keep their role, label and `aria-checked` and take `aria-disabled`, and drop out of the tab order.
- **The label is a `span`, deliberately.** There is no form control for a `label` element to point at, so the label has an id and the row is named by `aria-labelledby`.
- **`isRequired` marks the label and requires the group.** The asterisk follows the label and is read as "required"; the group carries the native required constraint.

## Related

- For a value on a longer scale, use Range.
- For a choice among labeled options rather than a score, use Radio group or Radio.
- For the comment that usually accompanies a rating, use Text area.

## Parts

1. **Label.** Text above the row that names the rating. A required marker follows it.
2. **Items.** Five 32 circles, each drawing a 16 icon. Items up to the score are filled.
3. **Number.** In the numeric variant, 1 to 5 above each item.
4. **Caption.** In the comments variant, one line under the row.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `--ds-background-neutral` circle with the icon outlined in `--ds-icon-subtle`. |
| Hovered | The item takes `--ds-background-neutral-hovered`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered look holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the item, for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | Icon is filled in `--ds-icon-selected`; unselected items are outlined in `--ds-icon-subtle`. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` fill and `--ds-icon-disabled` icon. Out of the tab order, still announced. |
| Invalid, read-only | Not drawn. Validate the answer in the form and explain the error beside the rating. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Item | `--item-height-md` (32) circle on `--ds-background-neutral`. |
| Icon | `--icon-md` (16). |
| Gaps | `--space-0625` between items; `--stack-sm` inside an item group; `--stack-md` between label and row, plus `--stack-sm` under the label. |
| Label, number | `--ds-text`, body default. |
| Required marker | `--ds-text-danger`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name what is rated, as a question: "How was the session?" | "Rating" alone, or an instruction: "Click a star." |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation except a question mark. | Title case. |
| Keep the comments caption to one short line. | A paragraph under the row. |
| Pair the rating with a comment box when you need the reason. | Ask for the reason in the label. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the star group, which the label names. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | Form key under which the chosen rating is sent with its form. |
| `label` | node | — | Visible label above the stars. It names the group; without one the group is named "Rating". |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Shows an asterisk on the label and marks the group required. |
| `value` | number | `0` | Current rating, 0 for none up to 5. Every star up to it is filled. Update it from `onChange`. |
| `variant` | enum | `'comments'` | `comments` (default) shows the icons alone, with an optional comments label under them; `numeric` prints each number above its icon. |
| `showCommentsLabel` | bool | `true` | Shows `commentsLabel` under the stars. Applies to the `comments` variant only. |
| `commentsLabel` | node | `'Comments'` | Text under the stars in the `comments` variant. Defaults to "Comments". |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disables every icon so no rating can be picked. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with the new rating (1 to 5) when the user picks a different star. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the wrapper around the label and stars. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the wrapper around the label and stars. |
| `icon` | enum | `'star'` | The glyph used for every choice: `star` (default) or `thumbs-up`. |
